subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker verification to native voice input, and should that live in core native app voice runtime or behind a plugin/provider API seam first?
rationale: The request is valid but it changes biometric state, voice authorization semantics, fallback behavior, config/storage surface, and possibly provider egress, so automation cannot choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Design native speaker gate first
options.body: Approve a narrow security-reviewed contract for one initial native voice flow, with canonical storage, threshold/fallback UX, and regression plus real-device proof before broad rollout.

options.title: Expose plugin/provider seam first
options.body: Keep core lean by designing only the missing extension point and letting speaker-verification implementations ship as plugins or ClawHub packages until a bundled reason is proven.

options.title: Defer speaker identity
options.body: Leave current wake-word, push-to-talk, and Talk behavior unchanged while documenting noisy-room mitigations until maintainers prioritize biometric voice identity.

recommendation.title: Design native speaker gate first
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow security-reviewed contract for one initial native voice flow, with canonical storage, threshold/fallback UX, and regression plus real-device proof before broad rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-main ownership signal for the central native macOS voice runtime files and are the best available routing owner for the product/security boundary choice.
